article.body_html:
A phone number on a booking works both ways: you reach the shop, and it can reach you when something changes, such as a bike that will not start, a return that is running late or a pickup time that has to move. A visitor may type whatever number is nearest to hand, such as a home number with roaming switched off or a chat account they only check on Wi-Fi. A number that cannot receive a call at 18:00 on a Hanoi street is not much of a contact. This guide helps you choose the number, and a backup, before you book.

Four ways to be reachable, and what each one needs

OptionWhat it needs to workWhere it can fail
Your home number on roamingRoaming switched on, credit or a plan that covers calls and textsRoaming may be switched off to avoid charges, and an unexpected call may be missed or declined
A local SIM or eSIMA SIM bought and activated, and the new number given to the shopSome tourist SIMs and eSIMs are data-only, with no number that rings; others can be set up only after you land, so the booking holds the old number until then
A messaging app accountMobile data or Wi-Fi, and notifications switched onMessages wait unread when the phone has no data, and the shop may use a different app
A second contact such as a hotel desk or a friendSomeone who agrees to pass messages onThe shop reaches a person who knows nothing about your trip unless you tell them

No single option wins on every point. The practical answer is to give two that fail in different ways.

Give a primary number and a backup

  • Primary: the way you are most likely to answer during the rental. Before arrival that may be your home number or an app account; once you have a local SIM, replace it.
  • Backup: one that does not depend on the same thing. If the primary depends on roaming, make the backup an app account that works on Wi-Fi; if the primary is an app, make the backup a number that rings.
  • Write the country code. Foreign numbers need the "+" and the country code so that the shop can dial them without guessing; give the Vietnamese number the same way, as +84, once you have one.

Test it before you rely on it

Send a message from the number you intend to give, to someone you know, and ask them to call back. Check that the call rings through instead of going to voicemail. If you plan to use an app, check that a message from a number the app does not know arrives as a notification and not a hidden request. If you are buying a local SIM, Vietnam SIM Card: Buy at Airport or City Shops? compares the places to buy one, and Vietnam eSIM for Tourists: Complete A-to-Z Guide to Buy and Activate covers the eSIM route. When you receive a new number, send it to the shop at once and ask it to confirm that it has replaced the old one.

Save the shop's number too

The contact works in both directions. Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà can be reached on 0334 699 969 (+84 334 699 969 from abroad), and the shop is open 09:00–21:00 daily. Save it under the shop's name before you leave the counter, and check that your phone can call a local number if you are on a foreign SIM. Ask the shop which channel it prefers for quick questions, since that is the one it is most likely to read in time. The shop's contact page is the place to check for any other way to reach it. If phone calls are not an option for you, say so when you book and ask for messages instead; Communicating a Hearing or Speech Access Need at Motorbike Pickup explains how to make the need clear.

When either side may need to call

  • A bike that will not start or has a warning on the dashboard.
  • A return that is running late. Hanoi Motorbike Breakdown After 21:00: Prepare a Safe Waiting Plan is a reminder that the shop's confirmed hours end at 21:00, so ask what to do if a problem starts after closing and keep a plan of your own.
  • A change to the time of a pickup or return.

For a bike that will not start, Rental Scooter Will Not Start: Information to Send the Shop lists what to note before you call. Never read, answer or return a call or message while riding: let it ring, pull over somewhere safe, and fit or adjust a mount only while stopped, as Phone Mounts on Rental Scooters: Compatibility and Distraction Checks explains.
